source: test fixture — issue #339 review round 5: the ORDER rung's refusal reaches a FOLDED chip, whose two sentences must still name one prescription once
description: drug-reference-combination-order-two-subjects.json with the second subject moved OUT of the partner's ATC subgroup and the rule's subject moved INTO it, so the one chip this arrangement raises is FOLDED (issue #88): Rifampicin J04AB02 shares J04AB with the partner's J04AB05 and also rules on it. The order's own combination code J04AC51 is not in the dataset, so DrugSafetyValidator.orderPartners falls to soleSubstanceOf, resolves J04AB05 to Rifapentine and OrderPartner.nameByOrder renames that partner after the ORDER. The display names Paracetamol, which the question also puts in play, so CoMedications.displayNamesAnotherChipSubject refuses the display for this co-medication. Returning null on that refusal left the rule sentence on partnerLabel while the class sentence kept classPartnerName's label, so ONE detail named one prescription two ways — issue #292's own invariant, broken by a refusal reason #292 did not have. Paracetamol carries no rule and shares no subgroup with the order's codes, so it raises no chip of its own and the arrangement is exactly one folded chip.

interactions.note: Both are rifamycins and induce CYP3A4.
